subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Ceylon Tea After Coffee Rust
description: One-minute skill: Ceylon Tea After Coffee Rust.

hook.text: When coffee rust destroyed Ceylon's plantations in the 1870s, Scottish planter James Taylor had an idea: tea.

buildup.text: Taylor planted tea on 19 acres in Kandy in 1867. His first shipment to London sold immediately.

discovery.text: Ceylon's climate and altitude were ideal. By 1890, tea covered the mountainsides where coffee once grew.

twist.text: Thomas Lipton bought failing coffee estates cheaply, converted them to tea, and built a global brand.

climax.text: Sri Lanka is now the world's fourth-largest tea exporter. Ceylon tea is a globally recognized name.

punchline.text: Coffee's disaster became tea's opportunity. Timing is everything.

quiz.question: Who turned failing Ceylon coffee estates into a global tea brand?

details.summary: When coffee leaf rust destroyed Ceylon's coffee plantations in the 1870s, planters pivoted to tea. Scottish planter James Taylor had already begun experimental tea cultivation. Within decades, Ceylon tea became world-renowned for quality.
details.whyItMatters: Ceylon's pivot from coffee to tea shows how agricultural disasters can create new industries. Sri Lanka's tea identity was born from a coffee crisis.
takeaways: Coffee rust in the 1870s destroyed Ceylon's coffee industry
James Taylor pioneered commercial tea cultivation in Ceylon
Sri Lanka remains one of the world's top tea producers

faq.question: How quickly did Ceylon switch from coffee to tea?
faq.answer: The transition took about two decades. Coffee rust first appeared in 1869 and by the 1890s, most former coffee estates had converted to tea. James Taylor's success at Loolecondera estate in 1867 proved tea was viable. By 1900, Ceylon was a major global tea exporter.

faq.question: What makes Ceylon tea distinctive?
faq.answer: Ceylon tea is known for bright, brisk, and medium-bodied character. The island's varied elevations produce different profiles: low-grown teas are strong and full, mid-grown are smooth and rich, and high-grown teas are light, floral, and prized. The variety is impressive for a small island.
